probe.command: make -n lint >/dev/null 2>&1 || make -n fmt >/dev/null 2>&1 || make -n format >/dev/null 2>&1

smoke.command: make --version >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 127; for t in lint fmt format; do make -n "$t" >/dev/null 2>&1 && exec make -n "$t"; done; exit 127

permissionRequirements: fallback: the Makefile target is the tool — nothing is installed, and a project with none of lint, fmt or format has no lint capability
fallback: the first target that resolves wins, in the order lint, fmt, format; the recipe never adds a target of its own
fallback: a dry run still expands the Makefile, so a variable defined through a shell call is evaluated when the target is read

maintenance.check: the recipe reads targets and dry-runs them; it breaks only if make drops -n or --version, so re-verify against the current make manual
